claim_boundary: Seven original video files contribute 157.9 reported seconds, not hundreds of independent sequence samples. The five folder labels cover advance, retreat, and lunge only; idle is documented but absent. The two broadcast files are unlabelled epee footage from one visual bout group. Evaluation must hold out complete visual source groups, and no athlete-generalisation claim is supported.

manual_visual_source_group_audit.note: Middle-frame inspection shows at least three visibly distinct training demonstrators, contradicting the README's single-fencer limitation. Both test clips show the same two-athlete Olympic epee bout and are one leakage group. These are conservative visual groups, not verified athlete identities.

rights_boundary: The README ends with a one-line MIT statement, but the pinned repository has no LICENSE file or full licence text and does not document the rights provenance of the Olympic broadcast clips. Raw videos, extracted frames, pose arrays, row-level metadata, and trained artefacts remain local; only adapter code, hashes, aggregate counts, and limitations are publishable.
upstream_validation_claim_not_adopted: The README's 97.14% validation accuracy is not treated as a benchmark result: the repository describes a 70/15/15 sequence split, source clips can generate overlapping windows, the bundled videos expose repeated demonstrators, and no frozen split or evaluation artefact is included.
